title: Supplemental New Zealand GIS research register: university research, claimant mapping, coastlines and national data infrastructure

stagingContext.instruction: Keep this register outside src/content. It is a reviewable research package and makes no edits to canonical records.

method.scope: Curated additions identified from institutional repositories, government sources, Tribunal records, research publications and professional material.
method.sourcePriority: Institutional repositories and primary government/organisation records first; peer-reviewed literature and independent research for interpretation and corroboration.
method.rights: Store bibliographic metadata and original paraphrased notes. Do not copy thesis/article full text into the project unless an item-specific licence explicitly permits the intended reuse. Link to repository-hosted files. For claimant evidence, check ownership, confidentiality, tikanga and claimant authority before reuse.
method.datePrecision: Use source publication date as listed; repository crawl or upload dates are not treated as publication dates.

findings.finding: CFRT describes GIS mapping as evidence support for eligible claimant groups: maps can combine chronological and geographic views of alienation, raupatu, purchases, development schemes, historic ownership, rohe, wāhi tapu and remaining Māori land. CFRT also states that claimant-supplied confidential information means many maps are not public; generic overview map books filed at the Tribunal may be public, while claimant-specific map books are claimant-owned.
findings.interpretation: Treat claimant mapping as a set of claimant-led, district and commissioned projects, not one national map programme. Respect the source's access and ownership conditions.

findings.finding: Waitangi Tribunal evidence identifies Te Matua Whenua / Land History and Alienation Database as a Central North Island inquiry resource. The Tribunal lists the 2005 evidence and a separate LHAD data bundle; the bundle is too large for website download and the Tribunal directs users to request a copy.
findings.interpretation: Do not describe LHAD as a complete national land-alienation database. Record its district and inquiry context unless further evidence establishes wider coverage.

findings.finding: The Opuatia GIS case study demonstrates a block-level method connecting Māori Land Court historic records with LINZ geospatial data. It reports substantial alienation and fragmentation, while explicitly identifying poor interoperability and archival research limits.
findings.interpretation: A strong proposed story is about reconstructing block histories by linking records, parcel/title structures and maps, alongside data sovereignty and interoperability limits.

findings.finding: LINZ's 3D Coastal Mapping programme began in late 2023 and runs through June 2027. It targets up to 40% of the coastline, nominally from 200 m inland of MHWS to 25 m water depth, using LiDAR and multibeam. The programme is baseline elevation mapping, not itself a sea-level-rise forecast.
findings.interpretation: Connect historical coastal GIS theses and risk studies to the current data programme, but distinguish observed terrain/bathymetry from scenario modelling, hazard probabilities and planning decisions.

findings.finding: LINZ describes the LDS as an online search, preview, download and API service for land and seabed datasets. Documented categories include imagery, elevation, topographic, hydrographic, property/boundary/ownership, place names, roads/addresses and Crown land. Current guidance documents OGC web services including WMTS and WFS.
findings.interpretation: Treat LDS as an access and publication platform; keep dataset custodian, platform/provider, licence and API access method as separate fields.

findings.finding: LINZ release documentation and the National Library's cartographic history support a distinct Topo50 story: the national 1:50,000 mapping series launched in 2009, with digital production and an updated reference framework.
findings.interpretation: Research the shift from NZMS 260 to Topo50 and how digital map production, georeferencing and LDS services changed access and reuse.

findings.finding: Koordinates sources identify Ed Corkery as the company's CEO. Separate Esri event material identifies an Ed Cook as a GIS Technical Solutions Consultant at Eagle Technology in an emergency-management presentation. Available evidence does not support identifying these as the same person or attributing Koordinates work to Ed Cook.
findings.interpretation: Keep two person candidates separate until primary biographical evidence supports any identity merge.

sourceRegister.title: NZ Research
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: DigitalNZ describes the portal as an index of New Zealand research outputs, including theses; the search result reported roughly 205,000 research objects, including about 44,000 masters-level records. Counts are dynamic and should be rechecked before publication.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Discovery metadata; follow each originating repository's terms.

sourceRegister.title: Developing a 3D Digital Cadastral Survey System for New Zealand
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Trent Frederick Douglas Gulliver; University of Canterbury
sourceRegister.type: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Examines New Zealand cadastral survey system requirements and proposes a conceptual approach to digital 3D cadastral capability.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository-hosted thesis PDF; link and cite. No project-wide licence established.

sourceRegister.title: The effect of a rise in mean sea level on the New Plymouth coastline: a GIS investigation
sourceRegister.type: MPhil in Geographic Information Systems thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses GIS with property and census datasets and a 3D coast/seabed model to investigate potential inundation and erosion/accretion scenarios; thesis abstract notes its scenario assumptions. It acknowledges LINZ data obtained through Koordinates.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Use repository record/search by exact title; no full-text redistribution rights established.

sourceRegister.title: Sea level rise: an assessment of risk, South Dunedin
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: The abstract states GIS methodology was integrated into a South Dunedin risk assessment; it gives scenario outputs but explicitly notes excluded compounding hazards and a dune-breach assumption. Those historical scenario results must not be presented as current forecasts.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Open-access thesis for research/private study; repository says copyright all rights reserved unless otherwise indicated. Link and cite; do not mirror thesis or maps.

sourceRegister.title: Decadal shoreline change on the New Zealand coast
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses GIS, orthorectified aerial photographs, 2011 GPS shoreline positions and Environment Canterbury beach profiles across four study sites. The repository says full text is unavailable/restricted; use the abstract and metadata only.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository marks full text unavailable/restricted; do not redistribute. Link and cite.

sourceRegister.title: Using Historic Satellite and 3D UAV Imagery to Map the Dynamics of the Coast at Sites with Anthropogenic Debris in Southland New Zealand
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Cassandra Newman; Auckland University of Technology
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses historical satellite imagery and seasonal 3D UAV imagery at four Southland sites to quantify shoreline and volumetric change; the repository identifies it as a 2022 Master of Science (Research) thesis.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Institutional repository record; link and cite.

sourceRegister.title: An exploration of the associations between urban natural environments and indicators of mental and physical health
sourceRegister.type: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis using GIS and a visibility-index method with individual-level NZ Health Survey data to examine natural-environment exposure and health indicators in Wellington.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Use repository record/search by exact title; no full-text redistribution rights established.

sourceRegister.title: A usability comparison of canvas, topographic and street base maps
sourceRegister.type: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis comparing canvas, topographic and street basemaps using an online survey and usability measures.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Use repository record/search by exact title; no full-text redistribution rights established.

sourceRegister.title: Characterising landscape and sea level dynamics to predict shoreline responses over the next 100+ years in a high energy tectonic setting, Kaikoura, New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Hannah Victoria Berger's 2017 MSc develops a conceptual framework for local coastal sediment dynamics and sea-level response, considering tectonics, climate and human intervention along the Kaikōura coast. The thesis notes sparse data constraints and should be read as a dated research scenario.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: UC repository states copyright/all rights reserved unless otherwise indicated; link and cite.

sourceRegister.title: A kawa led approach for the practical application of geospatial science
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Massey repository identifies an indefinitely embargoed 2023 MSc thesis. Its abstract discusses georeferencing historical Whanganui River maps, text extraction, iwi wellbeing indicators, story maps and data sovereignty.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Embargoed indefinitely: use repository metadata only and do not reproduce thesis content.

sourceRegister.title: Land Loss, Historic Trauma and the Intergenerational Transmission of Wellbeing: The Experience of Iwi ...
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses temporally informed Māori land/geospatial data and connects land loss history with wellbeing measures. Verify the complete title and award metadata before importing.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository record; link and cite. Confirm title/date discrepancies from deposited record.

sourceRegister.title: The benefits and barriers to GIS for Māori
sourceRegister.type: Master of Indigenous Planning and Development thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Kaupapa Māori research on potential benefits and barriers including access, capability, cost, cultural heritage and intellectual-property concerns. A DOC science report cites the thesis and gives its full title, award, year and length.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository PDF may be available; use metadata and original paraphrase, not copied thesis text.

sourceRegister.title: Report on the development and use of GIS for iwi and hapū: Motueka case study
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Graham Harmsworth, Ana Park and David Walker; Manaaki Whenua – Landcare Research
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Documents iwi/hapū GIS work in the Motueka region and examples concerning Te Ātiawa Treaty hearings and cultural impact assessment.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Public report PDF; rights for wholesale redistribution not confirmed. Link and paraphrase.

sourceRegister.title: He Whare Hangarau Māori: Language, culture & technology
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Includes Māori mapping and technology case studies, including Te Koronga mapping and the Indigenous Mapping Wānanga.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository lists Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International. Reuse only with attribution, noncommercial use and compliance with the licence; verify per chapter and any third-party material before copying.

sourceRegister.title: The Paepae: Spatial information technologies and the geography of narratives
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Research on spatial information technologies, narrative and Māori knowledge; use a stable repository record rather than temporary signed file links.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository item; verify stable handle and specific reuse rights before import.

sourceRegister.title: Ngā Mātāpono e Rua: Stories of co-creation for bicultural spatial governance in Aotearoa New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Examines co-creation and bicultural spatial governance, providing a conceptual and practice-oriented connection between mapping and governance.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Journal article; store citation and paraphrase only unless licence permits text reuse.

sourceRegister.title: The alienation of the Opuatia block: A GIS case study report written for Counting our Tūpuna
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Jesse Whitehead; National Institute of Demographic and Economic Analysis, University of Waikato
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Combines Māori Land Court historical alienation records with LINZ spatial data to analyse fragmentation and ownership change since 1866; report identifies source interoperability barriers and archival limits.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository-hosted report; link and cite. No project-wide full-text redistribution permission established.

sourceRegister.title: Tracing Opuatia: Repatriating and repurposing colonial land data
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Tahu Kukutai et al.; New Zealand Geographer
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Discusses repatriating and repurposing colonial land data, including the Opuatia case and links among Māori Land Court records, LINZ parcel/title material and survey plans; foregrounds data access and sovereignty.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Store bibliographic metadata and a short original summary; check article-level licence before reproducing any text or figures.

sourceRegister.title: Research activities
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Describes eligible-claimant mapping services, uses of maps in evidence and settlement negotiations, examples of mapped issues, and the distinction between public overview map books and claimant-owned/confidential maps.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Organisation's web content; quote only within fair dealing/fair use limits and link to the source.

sourceRegister.title: Aratohu mō ngā Rōpū Kaitono / Guide for Claimants Negotiating Treaty Settlements
sourceRegister.publishedAt: 2018 (PDF upload path; confirm document title page)
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Explains how map books can connect technical research and traditional history, and describes GIS mapping support and categories of events and places that may be mapped.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Link and paraphrase; check permission before reproducing figures or substantial text.

sourceRegister.title: Search Inquiry Documents: Te Matua Whenua – The Land History and Alienation Database evidence and data
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Lists David Alexander's 2005 evidence, follow-up evidence and LHAD data. The catalogue states the data bundle is too large for website download and must be requested.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Follow Tribunal access instructions; data bundle not publicly downloadable from this listing.

sourceRegister.title: Report to Appointors 2001/2002
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Describes Te Matua Whenua as a database project in the Central North Island context, intended to describe land alienation and support detailed maps.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Link and paraphrase.

sourceRegister.title: Insurance retreat in residential properties from future sea level rise in Aotearoa New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses spatial exposure analysis involving LINZ coastline and extreme sea-level inundation scenarios to assess residential insurance retreat. Cite the paper for its stated assumptions and scope.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Store citation and paraphrase only unless article licence allows broader reuse.

sourceRegister.title: Recent and future higher sea levels in New Zealand: A review
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Reviews observed and projected higher sea levels for New Zealand; useful historical context, not a substitute for current hazard projections.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Metadata and paraphrase only unless licence permits text reuse.

sourceRegister.title: The programme – 3D Coastal Mapping
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.publishedAt: programme started late 2023; page current at access
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Programme duration through June 2027; up to 40% of coastline; nominal mapping extent 200 m inland from MHWS to 25 m water depth; LiDAR and multibeam.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Link and attribute LINZ data separately from LINZ explanatory page content.

sourceRegister.title: LINZ Data Service
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Describes search, preview, download and API access and the main categories of land and seabed data available through LDS.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Dataset-level metadata and licence must be checked for each layer.

sourceRegister.title: Web services and versions and version support
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Documents LDS API and OGC service options; current version guidance includes WMTS, WFS and CS-W. API keys and specific service limits apply.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Technical documentation; link. Do not treat API access as permission to ignore layer terms.

sourceRegister.title: Licensing and using data
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Almost all LDS data is CC BY 4.0, but aerial imagery, personal-information layers and some other exceptions have distinct terms or additional access requirements.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Apply the specific dataset licence and attribution; do not assume every LDS layer has identical terms.

sourceRegister.title: Topo50 release notes and update history
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.publishedAt: undated; update history current at access
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Provides a maintained record of Topo50 map and dataset changes.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Link and attribute LINZ datasets separately.

sourceRegister.title: A history of topographic mapping in New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: National Library cartographic history is a discovery lead for the NZMS 260 to Topo50 transition and NZTM history; exact history page permalink remains to be pinned before public import.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Link and paraphrase; identify a stable page URL before publication.

sourceRegister.title: About Koordinates
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Koordinates company page identifies Ed Corkery as CEO. Koordinates' own 2013 account states that LDS was built using Koordinates Enterprise and supported by its engineers; treat this as a company account and corroborate with LINZ records.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Company source; link and paraphrase.

sourceRegister.title: New Zealand GIS for Emergency Management
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Esri event / Eagle Technology and Fire and Emergency New Zealand presenters
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: A StoryMaps event item among a set of GIS emergency-management presentations; this lead requires the title, authors and event date to be read from the presentation before public import.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Presentation material; link only until item-specific reuse permissions are known.

sourceRegister.title: LINZ Annual Report 2020/21
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Toitū Te Whenua Land Information New Zealand
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: LINZ annual reporting says the LINZ Data Service launched on 1 July 2011 and describes Koordinates as its platform provider; use LINZ's first-party account and pinpoint the specific report page before importing.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Government report; link and paraphrase.

sourceRegister.title: Geospatial Analysis of Marine Habitat Representation for Marine Spatial Planning Around Waiheke Island Auckland New Zealand
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Levi Murdoch-Tighe; Auckland University of Technology
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Uses mapped habitat, GIS, multivariate analysis and Marxan models to explore representative marine protected-area options and participatory management around Waiheke.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository item includes an item-specific licence. Link and cite; inspect licence before reuse of text, figures or data.

sourceRegister.title: Sand Dune Vegetation Monitoring and Assessment Using UAV Remote Sensing: A Case Study for Karekare Beach Auckland Region New Zealand
sourceRegister.authorOrganisation: Joshua Glyn Bilkey; Auckland University of Technology
sourceRegister.type: Master of Geographic Information Science thesis
sourceRegister.relevantEvidence: Compares UAV remote-sensing and vegetation-classification approaches for dune monitoring at Karekare; describes OBIA and pixel-based accuracy and notes invasive pampas grass classification.
sourceRegister.rightsAndReuse: Repository item; link and cite. Confirm item-specific licence before reusing figures or text.

proposedResearchRecords.title: The alienation of the Opuatia block: a GIS case study
proposedResearchRecords.summary: A research publication pair on reconstructing Māori land-block history by linking historical land records to current geospatial structures, while documenting data interoperability and governance limitations. Additional university leads connect coastal GIS to marine habitat planning and dune-vegetation monitoring.
connectionsToReview: Māori Land Court records — source material used

proposedResearchRecords.title: Mapping land history for Treaty claim research
proposedResearchRecords.summary: Explain claimant-led and commissioned map books, the distinct role of CFRT, the Central North Island LHAD, Māori GIS capability research, and the legal, ethical and data-access limits on reuse.
connectionsToReview: Crown Forestry Rental Trust — commissioned/funded support where source confirms
claimant groups — owners/users; name only from specific records

proposedResearchRecords.title: From sea-level scenarios to a national coastal elevation baseline
proposedResearchRecords.summary: Trace the evolution from local GIS risk and shoreline studies to present coastal elevation and bathymetric mapping, keeping terrain data, hazard modelling and insurance/planning interpretation distinct.

proposedResearchRecords.title: Topo50, Koordinates and the LINZ Data Service
proposedResearchRecords.summary: Explain national topographic map history and how the LDS made authoritative land/seabed data discoverable and accessible through downloads and APIs; separate LINZ data custody from Koordinates platform services.

proposedResearchRecords.title: Māori geospatial practice and governance reading collection
proposedResearchRecords.summary: A bibliographic collection spanning Māori GIS capability, iwi/hapū practice, cultural mapping, spatial narratives, kawa-led geospatial work and bicultural spatial governance.

relationshipRegister.subject: Crown Forestry Rental Trust
relationshipRegister.basis: CFRT annual report and Tribunal evidence catalogue; scope is Central North Island inquiry context, not national coverage.

relationshipRegister.object: Māori Land Court historical records and LINZ geospatial information
relationshipRegister.basis: Report abstract explicitly identifies these source classes.

relationshipRegister.subject: LINZ
relationshipRegister.basis: Current LINZ service description and annual report. Koordinates platform role is separately attributed.

identityAndEvidenceReview.detail: Ed Corkery is identified by Koordinates as CEO. Ed Cook appears in emergency-management GIS presentation material in an Eagle Technology role. No evidence found tying Ed Cook to Koordinates.

identityAndEvidenceReview.issue: Land History and Alienation Database scope
identityAndEvidenceReview.detail: Evidence is tied to Te Matua Whenua and the Central North Island inquiry. Do not imply nationwide coverage.
CFRT states many maps use confidential information and claimant-specific map books are claimant-owned. Public visibility in a Tribunal record does not itself establish unrestricted reuse rights.
Most LDS data is CC BY 4.0, but imagery, personal-information layers and pending-approval cadastral data may have different terms or access requirements.

gapsAndNextResearch: This is a curated expansion, not an exhaustive census of all NZ university GIS theses. Use DigitalNZ/NZ Research and each university repository for a systematic subject-and-year sweep.
Find and verify New Zealand university research on CFRT commissioned map books, Tribunal evidence mapping and LHAD implementation, with claimant ownership and access terms recorded per item.

Build a layer-by-layer LDS register with layer ID, authoritative custodian, revision history, geometry/scale, update schedule, API endpoints, licence and documented downstream use. Current register captures service-level categories, not every layer.
Pinpoint historical Topo50 and LDS annual-report citations and the exact Esri event page before converting those leads into public story claims.

Expand sea-level research across regional council hazard assessments, NIWA scenarios, MfE guidance, local planning instruments, adaptation programmes and community mapping; distinguish model assumptions and vertical datums.
Search Survey and Spatial New Zealand, Spatial News, NZ Esri user-group newsletters and conference proceedings for work not indexed in university repositories.
Remaining exact repository leads should be converted from discovery results to stable item permalinks before any public import; do not substitute institution homepages for a record citation.

contentHandling.replicate: Bibliographic records, URLs, dates, repository identifiers, original short summaries, access notes, rights metadata and source-backed relationship proposals are stored here.
contentHandling.doNotReplicate: Do not copy complete copyrighted thesis/article PDFs, figures, claimant map books, personal information or confidential cultural information into the site repository without specific permission/licence and appropriate claimant authority.
contentHandling.publicationGate: Before public import, resolve medium-confidence citations, check existing record IDs and names in canonical data, map each claim to a pinpoint citation, and validate licence, cultural authority, date precision and relationships.
